title: Striking star clusters and irregular clumps
caption: The irregular galaxy Arp 263, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: constellation Leo · about 25 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #13 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A broad band of tiny stars, denser on one side, is dotted with clumps of new stars wrapped in glowing blue gas, while plumes of red dust surround it. This is Arp 263, also catalogued as NGC 3239, an irregular galaxy about 25 million light-years away in Leo, seen by Webb's Near-Infrared Camera.

Arp 263 is believed to be the product of a past merger. It has two short, curved tails of stars, its stars are oriented differently from its hydrogen gas, and parts of that gas move at different speeds. Widespread star birth also hints that its gas has been badly stirred. The former partner, however, is nowhere to be found. It may have been a dwarf galaxy already dissolved, or one far heavier than it was bright.

Webb looks inside the thick gas to show older stars scattered through the galaxy beside busy nurseries. The most intense region features a curved chain of compact clusters leading to the brightest nebula.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.20 x 2.22 arcminutes) and distance (25 million light years), the frame spans roughly 16,000 × 16,000 light-years. Its light set out about 25 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam observed in near-infrared light. Blue and cyan mark shorter wavelengths including glowing hydrogen gas, green a water-ice filter, and red the glow of complex dust molecules (PAHs).
understand.eye: All of this light is near-infrared and invisible to the eye, and it lets Webb look inside the thick gas crowding the galaxy.

explore: The brightest spot in the frame is a star in our own Milky Way, which is why it looks so large and has long diffraction spikes. Hundreds of far more distant galaxies show up behind it as orange dots. The data come from programme #3707, a survey of nearby star-forming galaxies in the southern sky. Halton Arp listed the galaxy in his 1966 atlas of peculiar galaxies.
alt: A broad, irregular band of tiny stars with bright clumps wrapped in blue gas, red dust plumes, a large bright foreground star and a few background galaxies.
